picks.title: How Charli XCX's producers ran a jam session through an AI sampling plugin to make No One Lasts Forever
picks.excerpt: A. G. Cook and Finn Keane describe on the Tape Notes podcast how they ran a chaotic studio jam through Concatenator, an AI-powered concatenative-synthesis sampling plugin that turns arbitrary sample material into a playable instrument, to build the track's texture.
picks.rationale: A named-record, step-by-step account of AI sampling used as a texture engine — the rare craft story a producer can copy in their own session tomorrow.

picks.title: Peel Stems 2 from zplane
picks.excerpt: zplane's real-time stem-separation plug-in cuts processing latency from 483ms to 245ms at 44.1kHz with cleaner separation and fewer artefacts, running natively in VST3/AU/AAX with no cloud upload, subscription or login.
picks.rationale: Halved latency plus fully local processing turns AI stem separation from an offline chore into a live, in-session tool — a concrete workflow upgrade.

picks.title: Sony Music sues Udio for a second time, with the extra 30,000 recordings that could result in $4.5 billion damages
picks.excerpt: After a judge refused to let Sony amend its original complaint, the label filed a fresh action over 30,000+ additional recordings — an expanded list that could expose Udio to more than $4.5 billion in statutory damages.
picks.rationale: The one major label still without a Udio deal escalates to existential damages — a direct signal on whether Udio stays a safe tool to build releases on.

picks.title: SOCAN and Musical AI to Track (and Eventually Pay) Creators for AI Use
picks.excerpt: Canada's largest rights organisation is building attribution infrastructure with Musical AI to detect when members' works influence AI-generated output, establishing consent mechanisms and a route to eventual royalty payments.
picks.rationale: First real attribution plumbing from a major PRO — the mechanism by which training influence could actually become a royalty line for working writers.

picks.title: AI artists are already making millions from Spotify and YouTube – and they're only getting bigger
picks.excerpt: New analysis puts the top ten AI acts at roughly $6.1 million in combined earnings, with audiences in the tens of millions, hundreds of chart entries and major playlist placements — evidence AI music has moved from novelty to a real revenue tier.
picks.rationale: Hard revenue and chart numbers replace speculation: AI acts are now a competitive tier that human artists share playlists and payouts with.
